request: A dialogue quiz: three famous names that lie. How long was the Hundred Years' War, where are Panama hats made, where are guinea pigs from? #interactive #short
subtitle: Three famous names, three fibs: guess how long the Hundred Years' War lasted, where Panama hats are made and where guinea pigs come from.

spec.title: Do these names tell the truth?

sources.title: Hundred Years' War
sources.finding: intermittent conflict between England and France, 1337-1453

sources.title: Traditional weaving of the Ecuadorian toquilla straw hat
sources.finding: the so-called Panama hat is woven in Ecuador from toquilla palm fibre; inscribed on the Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2012

sources.title: Guinea pig
sources.finding: a South American rodent, domesticated in the Andes thousands of years ago; still raised for food there

sources.title: National Guinea Pig Day (Día Nacional del Cuy)
sources.authors: Peru, Ministry of Agriculture (reported by TreXperience Peru)
sources.finding: since 2013 Peru marks National Cuy Day on the second Friday of October, with fairs and festivals promoting breeding and eating guinea pigs

card.title: Do these names tell the truth?

commands.speak: Three famous names, and every one of them tells a fib. Can you spot where?
First, the Hundred Years' War, between England and France.

quiz.question: How long did the Hundred Years' War last?
quiz.right: A hundred and sixteen years: England and France fought on and off from 1337 to 1453.

commands.speak: A hundred and sixteen? I'd have said a hundred, obviously.
Next one. The Panama hat. Surely that one's safe?

quiz.question: So where are Panama hats really made?
quiz.right: Ecuador. They are woven from toquilla palm straw, around towns like Montecristi and Cuenca.

commands.speak: They were shipped out through Panama, and the workers who dug the canal wore them.
And the guinea pig. At least that's from Guinea?

quiz.question: Where do guinea pigs come from?
quiz.right: The Andes of South America, where people tamed them thousands of years ago, and still eat them today.

commands.speak: So not from Guinea at all. Peru even gives it a national day every October, with fairs and feasts.
You got {score} of {score_total}. Three names, three fibs.
As for the guinea pig: it's a rodent. It just squeals a bit like a piglet.

feedback.good: You saw through most of them.
feedback.poor: These names have fooled people for centuries.
